method: Per-epic Sonnet reviewers against six prototype maps, each review re-checked by an adversarial Sonnet verifier; plus a verified data-model delta and a verified reverse check.

epics.title: Contracts
epics.observations: Structural: EP-04's shell is the main gap. Contracts, Parties and Funding tags are three Billing views inside Master data (masterViews.ts, ?view=contracts|parties|fundingTags) opening side panels. The catalogue now wants a Contracts section of the Admin app with its own nav entry, a page per Contract with separately saved cards, a New contract page, a grouped catalogue with an index, Parties and Funding tags as tabs, a Party page, and a Replace-from-a-date action (phases 45 to 49). The step rail (US-04.3.8), backstops (US-04.3.9) and funding-tag placement (US-04.2.17) already match, and their open questions (OQ-145, OQ-146) are consistent with current behaviour. Verification changed one detail: the price range table already shows each range's end inside its 'In force' cell (rangeSpanText), so only a To column, Change column, Procedures-priced count, newest-first order and the fold after three are missing. Domain support is largely in place: partyRefusal, billingDetailsRefusal, fundingTagRefusal, contractRefusal (incl. holderBillingDetails), nextAaCode, rangeInForce, rangeSpanText, proceduresStillOnContract (skips authorised Lists), contractDisabledOn, destinationOf, the contractDisabled review flag, and audit actions for Party, Contract, price range, specialty, funding tag and RVG group. New work: a stored replace link and date (Contract has no date field, so likely an audited entry or a new field with a PERSIST_VERSION bump), a replaceContract store action that copies the Contract, moves ticked Procedures with audit, and either leaves the old Contract active or disables it; a to-do or warning rule on the change date (nothing under domain/warnings/rules; WarningsToDo is the Day view surface); a late-disable listing from the stored change date (reuse proceduresStillOnContract); a disable-confirm step that lists Procedures from today; a similar-name hint; per-card save with one audit entry each (editContract today writes one whole-Contract contract.update); a Procedures-on-the-Contract list (upcoming and authorised at locked price; lockedAgainstContract covers only the authorised half); a read-only Party billing block; per-range Procedures-priced counts and the fold; Party counts by funding tag; grouping facets (holder, kind of holder, tag, surgeon incl. two-surgeon Contracts under both, destination, pricing kind) with an index. Demo triggers: the existing advanceClockToDate store action (clockActions.ts, used by the prepayment trigger) makes the 'reach the change date' button cheap; the demo-backdated-range trigger's `when` (registry.ts:1894, reads adminMasters.view and adminContracts.openContractId) must follow the new section, and the old ?view=contracts|parties|fundingTags URLs need redirects (parseMastersView in screens/masters/view.ts). Demo guide: S1 to S5 do not use the Contracts master (S1 Beat 3 and the phone beat use the unchanged shared rail), but docs/demo-guide/03-demo-script.md:113 links ?view=contracts&holder=PY-COS and demoGuideSync.test.ts must stay green; the catalogue screenshots show the retired dated model and are left to the owner's /sweep. All ten items are status Verify (3) and the late-disable rule, the to-do on the date and future-dated disable (OQ-144) are not yet discussed with AA.

epics.title: RVG master data and fee calculation rules
Admin oversight and master data
epics.observations: Both items are the Master data side of Donald's 25 Nov Contracts-section decision. Closing them is mostly moving the Contracts, Parties and Funding tags views out of Master data into a new Contracts section (phases 45 and 48 of the brief), plus a Contracts-under-a-tag panel on the Funding tags tab, grouped by hospital with counts. Dependencies: US-04.1.7, US-04.1.8 and US-04.1.2 own the new section, Contract page, New contract page, grouped catalogue and Replace from a date. Structural touch points: the masterViews.ts registry and masterViews.test.ts catalogue-row mapping, redirects for old ?view=contracts, ?view=parties and ?view=fundingTags links, the Party 'active' link (?view=contracts&holder=), the demo-trigger contexts adminMasters.view and adminContracts.openContractId, the Seed load and Go-live entity sheets (contracts, priceRanges, parties, fundingTags), and the Admin SideNav and AdminApp sectionForPath. Funding tag behaviour (order, funder, audited changes, Suggested path via the rail) works today and must be preserved. No new demo trigger is needed; the existing demo-backdated-range trigger on Contracts should follow the move. The demo guide and screenshots (US-13.4.1 images admin-master-data-contracts*, -parties and -funding-tags; US-13.4.5 images) change path with the move, but they are left to the owner's /sweep and not edited per phase. I did not read the demo script, so I do not name the beats.

The add/edit sheet has Code and a Funder select grouped by Party kind. Order drives the step rail (fundingTagsInOrder). Funder naming feeds the rail's Suggested marker (shared/contracts/railParts.tsx, domain/billing/contractRail.ts funderPartyId). Changes go through mutate() and are audited, with a History sheet.

dataModelDeltas.title: A Contract remembers which Contract it replaces, and from when
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: US-04.1.8: the late disable lists the Procedures dated from the date of the change, and an old Contract left Active gets a to-do on that date, so the change date must be known after the action. US-04.1.2 'No dates': a Contract has no start, end or review date of its own (domain-model.md: 'None of these settings is dated'). OQ-144 (open) asks whether a Contract may get a date. US-04.1.3: a replacement is audited. domain-model.md does not mention the link, so US-04.1.8 is the only authority.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: The link exists only as two useState values in the New contract panel (replacesId, replacesFrom), used to show a warn-only list once and then lost. Contract has no replaces or replaced-by field, createContract takes no replaces input, and the contract.create audit entry does not name the old Contract. Nothing records afterwards that a Contract was replaced or from what day.
dataModelDeltas.impact: DM-02, DM-03 and DM-04 all need the change date after the fact, so this must precede them. Home: the audit route fits the 'no dates' rule and OQ-144 best (the new Contract's contract.create entry carries replaces {contractId, fromISO} in its after; no Contract field, no PERSIST_VERSION bump from 78). The date must be an explicit payload field because it is the office's chosen date, not the save time that disabledDaysByContract reads from the entry timestamp. The alternative, a replacedBy {contractId, fromISO} field on the old Contract, is a date on the Contract, needs a bump and a seed scenario. One derived read, 'the Contract this one replaced and from which day' (and the reverse), feeds the other three deltas.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Relationship and need upheld. Corrected the home: the audit route is not 'the way disabledDaysByContract reads the day' (that reads the entry timestamp; the change date is user-entered, so it needs a payload field), and a Contract field would put a date on the Contract against 'No dates' while OQ-144 is open. Noted domain-model.md has no statement of the link.

dataModelDeltas.title: Replace a Contract from a date, as one action
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: US-04.1.8 (new): one action creates a new Contract copied from the old with any setting changed (the settings fixed at creation included), lists the Procedures dated on or after the date still on the old Contract, moves only the ones the office ticks (each an audited Procedure change, authorised Lists locked and not listed), then leaves the old Contract Active with a to-do or disables it at once. A non-fixed replacement is offered from the day it is saved; a system Contract cannot be replaced. US-04.1.2 and US-04.1.3 point to it; a fixed price changing from a date is a price range, not a replacement (US-04.2.15). US-04.1.7 lists a Contract's event fees on its page.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Two separate acts: the office creates a new Contract by hand, optionally naming the one it replaces and a date, and the panel shows a read-only list of Procedures still on the old one. Nothing copies the old Contract, nothing moves Procedures from the panel (each move is a separate setProcedureContract on its own Booking, which has no planner and calls mutate() itself with side effects: clears typed price and rail answers, may re-open a completed Booking, may settle a prepayment), and the old Contract is neither left with a to-do nor disabled as part of it. The list already excludes authorised Lists and cancelled Bookings but not removed Draft Lists (proceduresStillOnContract). A Contract's event fees are separate records (masters.contractEventFees) that planContractCreate does not copy.
dataModelDeltas.impact: New office-only store action: create the copy (planContractCreate is the create half, runs contractRefusal, new AA code, DM-01 link), move exactly the ticked Procedures through the existing Contract change path, then leave or disable the old Contract (move first, then disable). Open points for the phase: setProcedureContract is not plan-shaped, so 'one action' is a sequence of per-Procedure commits or a refactor to a planner; per-row refusal outcomes are needed (contractPickRefusal can refuse when the copy changes holder, links or specialties, and removed Draft Lists are listed but unmovable); whether the copy carries event fees is not stated; a system Contract is refused. Depends on DM-01; carries the New contract page's replace entry and supersedes the warn-only list on create.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Upheld as a new lifecycle. Added what the author missed: setProcedureContract has no planner and carries side effects, the removed-Draft-List gap in the still-on list, and event fees as separate records not covered by the copy. Corrected line refs (ContractEditSheet 138, planContractCreate 169).

dataModelDeltas.title: A Contract still Active after its replacement date is a to-do item
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: US-04.1.8: when the old Contract is left Active, on the change date a to-do reminds the office to disable it, and the old Contract stays offered until it does. FT-13.7 and US-13.7.2: the dashboard to-do list. OQ-144 (open): the to-do stands in until a Contract can be disabled from a future date.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: The to-do list has two row kinds, both keyed to a Booking: open warnings and Bookings with no Contract (ToDoItem). Warning carries a bookingId and WarningFacts is one Booking, so no rule can take a Contract as subject. No to-do row concerns a Contract and none depends on a date passing. The noContract rows show only on the Admin Day rail's work card, which opens rows through onOpenBooking only.
dataModelDeltas.impact: A third ToDoItem kind with a Contract subject, derived (not stored) from the DM-01 link once the demo clock reaches the change date while the old Contract is still Active, leaving the list when the office disables it. Follows the noContract row's pattern (a work list, no Clear) on the rail's work card, not the warning routine or its clearance store. toDoItems ordering needs a rule for a row with no session; the rail card needs a way to open a Contract (the row opens the old Contract's page); whether a re-enabled old Contract brings the row back is unstated. No persisted state. Needs DM-01.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Catalogue statement and prototype gap confirmed in code. Added the rail card's navigation limit, the re-enable edge and the line refs; nothing about the delta changed.

dataModelDeltas.title: Disabling is confirmed and lists the Procedures first
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: US-04.1.2 'Disable confirmed': the office confirms a disable and is shown the Procedures dated from today still on the Contract. US-04.1.8: a late disable of a replaced Contract lists the Procedures from the change date, not only from that day on; 'Old one disabled' disables as it is replaced. The review flag for a Procedure dated on or after the disable day (US-07.2.2) is unchanged.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Disable is one click that sets status disabled at once (toggleStatus, disableContract). The Procedures still on it are listed only afterwards, on the disabled Contract's panel, from the disable day (stillOnContract with disabledDay or today). No confirmation step and no list before the change.
dataModelDeltas.impact: The list moves ahead of the change, from today by default, and from the DM-01 change date when the Contract was replaced and is disabled after that date. No store invariant changes (a Procedure on a Disabled Contract keeps it; the review flag still keys on the audit's disable day, so a Procedure dated between the change date and the disable day is listed but not flagged, as the criterion expects), so the confirm step is the existing read proceduresStillOnContract with a different fromISO, plus the 'disable as it is replaced' path DM-02 calls. The post-disable listing can go. Shares the list component and fromISO choice with DM-02. Needs DM-01 only for the replaced case.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Confirmed: disable is one click with the list shown only afterwards. Added that the flag/list difference for the late disable is intended by the criterion, and the shared list with DM-02.

deltaSummary:
All four deltas survived; none dropped and none added. I updated /Users/d.fraser/Development/Stratos Dev/AnaesthesiaAssociatesRFP/docs/build-plan/analysis/domain-model-delta.md to match.

DM-01 is corrected. The relationship and the need are real. The home needed fixing, because the change date is chosen by the office. The existing `disabledDaysByContract` reads the audit entry's timestamp, which is the save time, so the replacement's audit entry needs an explicit `replaces {contractId, fromISO}` field. A `fromISO` field on the Contract would be a date on the Contract. That sits against US-04.1.2 "No dates" and the open OQ-144. So the audit route is recommended, with no persist bump and no seed change needed. `domain-model.md` does not describe the link, so US-04.1.8 is its only authority.

DM-02 is corrected. I added three points the author missed:
- `setProcedureContract` has no planner. It calls `mutate()` itself and has side effects: it clears the typed price and rail answers, can re-open a completed Booking, and can settle a prepayment. "One action" is therefore a run of per-Procedure commits, or a refactor into a planner.
- The still-on list does not exclude removed Draft Lists, but those Procedures cannot be moved.
- Event fees are separate records (`masters.contractEventFees`) that the create planner does not copy. The stories leave open whether the copy carries them.

I also corrected two line refs and noted that the old Contract must be moved from first, then disabled.

DM-03 and DM-04 are upheld, with notes added. For DM-03, the rail's work card opens rows only as Bookings and needs a way to open a Contract. Whether a re-enabled old Contract brings the to-do back is unstated. For DM-04, the late-disable list and the review flag differ on purpose, as the criterion expects, and the list is shared with DM-02.

I also re-checked the author's "no delta" list. The Contract page, grouped list, Parties and Funding tags tabs, and price-range table are screens over data that already exists. The holder-fixed rule is already enforced in the prototype.
